extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality standards for the parts, form, and content of U.S. patent applications, including inventorship, title, specification, fee payment, refunds, and related examiner practices under MPEP and CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending nonprovisional applications will be permitted to be amended by complying with 37 CFR 1.48 to add claims to inventions by inventors not named when the application was filed when such inventions were disclosed in the application as filed; 37 CFR 1.48 permits correction of inventorship where the correct inventor(s) are not named through error without deceptive intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are responsible for correcting inventorship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48 when claims are amended so that a named inventor is no longer an inventor of a remaining claim. The examiner should remind applicants to correct inventorship when restriction is required and an invention is elected and claims to other inventors are canceled. Examiner should not inquire about inventors/invention dates until necessary for proper examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) and interplay with 35 U.S.C. 116
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 116, an examiner may reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) only where a named inventor is not the inventor of at least one claim in the application; no rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) is appropriate if a named inventor made a contribution to the invention defined in any claim of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered with 35 U.S.C. 103(c), a rejection may be appropriate under 102(f)/103 where the prior art and the claimed invention were not owned by, or subject to obligation of assignment to, the same person at the time the invention was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of common ownership for joint inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed with joint inventors, the examiner should assume that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time the inventions were made, unless there is evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventors not commonly owned at time of later invention file a joint application, applicants must pursuant to 37 CFR 1.56 point out inventor and invention dates and the lack of common ownership so the examiner can consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103, 102(f)/103, or 102(g)/103. The examiner should assume applicants comply with their duty of disclosure unless evidence indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 119(a) foreign priority/benefit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 119(a) benefit may be claimed to any foreign application so long as the U.S. named inventor was the inventor of the foreign application invention and 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) requirements are met. One condition is that the foreign application must be for 'the same invention' as the U.S. application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining two or more foreign applications in a single U.S. application, the U.S. application may claim benefit to each foreign application provided 119(a)-(d) requirements are met. A claim relying on a combination of prior foreign applications may not be entitled to benefit if the claim's subject matter was not sufficiently disclosed in the prior foreign application(s). Example illustrated (A invents X, B invents Y, combine X+Y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title length and placement (37 CFR 1.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention may not exceed 500 characters in length and must be as short and specific as possible. Unless supplied in an application data sheet, the title should appear as a heading on the first page of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters not capturable by the Office's automated systems may not be reflected in Office records. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive; place at top of first page unless provided in ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title content conventions and prohibited leading words
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive and should contain fewer than 500 characters. Words 'new,' 'improved,' 'improvement of,' 'improvement in' are not considered part of the title and should not be included at the beginning; the articles 'a,' 'an,' and 'the' should not be included as the first words and will be deleted when entered into Office computer records or when patent issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title is not descriptive of the invention claimed, examiner should require substitution of a new title clearly indicative of the invention; if applicant does not supply satisfactory title, examiner may change title at allowance (examiner's amendment). Use form paragraphs 6.11 and 6.11.01 when requiring a title change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require change in title and suggested change practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the title is not descriptive of the invention claimed, the examiner should require substitution of a new title that is clearly indicative of the invention to which the claims are directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.11 (Title of Invention Is Not Descriptive) and 6.11.01 (Title of Invention, Suggested Change) may be used. If changing title, indicate change on file label or bib-data sheet and follow IFW/TC procedures for examiner's amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing, search, and examination fees (37 CFR 1.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application filing fees are set under 35 U.S.C. 41 and listed in 37 CFR 1.16. For nonprovisional applications filed on or after Dec 8, 2004, basic filing, search, and examination fees (and application size/excess claims fees if applicable) are required; for older filings different fee rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are due on filing but may be paid later within time periods set by 37 CFR 1.53(f) (and surcharges may apply). Specific transitional rules apply for applications filed in particular date ranges; provisional and international national-stage applications have their own fee references (e.g., 37 CFR 1.492 for national stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application size fee applies when the specification (including claims) and drawings, excluding sequence listings or computer program listings in compliant electronic media, exceed 100 sheets of paper. The fee applies for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof over 100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings/computer program listings filed in electronic medium in compliance with rules are excluded. When submitted on electronic medium other than Office e-filing, each 3 kilobytes is counted as a sheet. For e-filed submissions, paper-size equivalent is 75% of the number of sheets when rendered by the Office e-filing system. Sequence listings in ASCII as associated file excluded; PDF/TIFF listings as part of specification/drawings are not excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees (37 CFR 1.16(h),(i),(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fee applies for each independent claim in excess of three (37 CFR 1.16(h)) and for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty (37 CFR 1.16(i)). A separate fee is required for an application containing a proper multiple dependent claim (37 CFR 1.16(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for multiple dependent claims are calculated based on the number of claims to which the multiple dependent claim refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)); improper multiple dependent claim charged as single dependent claim. Transitional rules apply for claims/fees across Dec 8, 2004. For reissue applications, original patent claims are not counted in determining excess claims fee for reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required with amendments affecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of an amendment (whether entered or not) affecting the claims, payment of fees for those claims in excess of the number previously paid for is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments before the first action, or not filed in reply to an Office action, presenting additional claims in excess of the number already paid for and not accompanied by full additional fee will not be entered and applicant will be advised. Such amendments filed in reply to an Office action will be regarded as not responsive thereto and MPEP § 714.03 practice followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of additional fees for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional fees due with an amendment are calculated on the basis of the claims (total and independent) which would be present if the amendment were entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment of a claim that does not change a dependent claim to independent, and replacement of a claim by a claim of the same type (unless a multiple dependent refers to more prior claims), do not require additional fees. Money paid for a proposed amendment will not be refunded because of nonentry of the amendment, but unentered claims will not be counted when calculating fees due in subsequent amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim treatment and improper dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For fee-determination purposes, a claim will be treated as dependent if it contains reference to one or more other claims. Any claim in dependent form that in fact is not a proper dependent claim (e.g., does not include every limitation of the claim on which it depends) must be canceled as not a proper dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of further claims depending on such improper dependent claim may be required. Applicant may amend the claims to place them in proper dependent form or redraft them as independent claims upon payment of any necessary additional fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of nonelected claims after restriction for fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: After a requirement for restriction, nonelected claims will be included in determining the fees due in connection with a subsequent amendment unless such claims are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment canceling claims accompanying the papers constituting the application will be effective to diminish the number of claims to be considered in calculating filing fees. Preliminary amendments filed with response to Notice To File Missing Parts that cancel/add claims will be taken into account in determining appropriate fees due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of applying insufficient payment for nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If payment submitted for fees on filing is insufficient and applicant does not specify allocation, Office will apply payment in the following order until expended: (1) basic filing fee; (2) application size fee; (3) late filing surcharge; (4) processing fee for non-English application; (5) search fee; (6) examination fee; (7) excess claims fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines how partial payments are allocated when applicant is silent; separate order provided for provisional applications: (1) basic filing fee; (2) application size fee; (3) late filing surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds / returnability of fees (37 CFR 1.26; 35 U.S.C. 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required. A change of purpose after payment (e.g., withdrawing a filing) will not entitle a party to a refund. The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless specifically requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds of credit card payments will be made by credit to the charged credit card account. Office may require banking information for EFT refunds. Questions about return of fees referred to Refunds Section of Receipts Division; do not express opinions to applicants about refundability—handle via petitions/official channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and procedures for requesting refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid, except as otherwise provided. For deposit-account charges made in an amount other than specifically indicated on authorization, refund requests must be filed within two years from date of deposit-account statement indicating such charge and include a copy of that statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For refunds based on later establishment of small entity status (37 CFR 1.28(a)), a three-month period applies. Receipt date treatment for deposit account charge authorization affects refund-period start date. Certificate of mailing/Express Mail date rules specified for refund timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: Office may obtain banking information necessary for making refunds by electronic funds transfer or obtain deposit-account information to make the refund to a deposit account; if not instructed otherwise, Office will attempt EFT. Refund of fees paid by credit card will be credited to the same card account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not cost effective to require banking info, Office may issue refund by treasury check. Refunds generally issued in form of original payment (e.g., check, EFT, deposit credit, or credit card credit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee upon express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Mar 10, 2006, Office may refund the search fee and any excess claims fee paid in an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after Dec 8, 2004, if applicant files a petition to expressly abandon the application before an examination has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basic filing fee, examination fee, and application size fee cannot be refunded unless the fee was paid by mistake or in excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement and specification content (37 CFR 1.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using the same, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention. The specification must set forth the precise invention for which a patent is solicited, distinguish it from other inventions and from what is old, describe a specific embodiment, and explain mode of operation or principle when applicable. The best mode contemplated by the inventor must be set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For improvements, specification must particularly point out parts of the process/machine/etc. to which improvement relates and be confined to the specific improvement and cooperating parts necessary for complete understanding. All amendments or claims must find descriptive basis in the original disclosure (no new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on offensive language and drawings (decorum and courtesy, 37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner notes language that could be deemed offensive to any race, religion, sex, ethnic group, or nationality, the examiner should object as failing to comply with the Rules of Practice; inclusion of such language or offensive depictions/caricatures in drawings should be similarly objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application should not be classified for publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) and an examiner should not pass the application to issue until such language or drawings have been deleted, or questions relating to propriety fully resolved. Basis also in public interest and Rules of Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formatting and sheet separation (37 CFR 1.71(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet. Each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application or other information. The claim(s), abstract and sequence listing (if any) should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may require papers to be printed, typewritten, or on an electronic medium. Follow sheet-separation rules to avoid mixing parts on same sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and mask work notice inclusion and required authorization wording
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in a design or utility patent application adjacent to copyright and mask work material contained therein. Inclusion permitted only if the authorization language (specified paragraph) is included at the beginning of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided example authorization wording that must appear (e.g., 'A portion of the disclosure of this patent document contains material which is subject to (copyright or mask work) protection...' etc.). For notices in drawings see § 1.84(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to disclose parties to joint research agreement (35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may disclose or be amended to disclose the names of the parties to a joint research agreement. An amendment under paragraph (g)(1) must be accompanied by the processing fee if not filed within one of specified time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted time windows to avoid processing fee: (i) within 3 months of filing date of national application; (ii) within 3 months of entry of national stage; (iii) before mailing of first Office action on the merits; (iv) before mailing of first Office action after filing of request for continued examination (RCE). If filed after issue fee paid, patent as issued may not include names — must correct by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323.
